contract_terms_summary: Guaranteed monthly uptime: target 99.95% (measured UTC calendar month)
Credit schedule proposed: uptime >=99.95% => no credit; 99.5%-99.95% => 10% monthly service credit; 99.0%-99.49% => 25% credit; <99.0% => 50% credit
Measurement window: rolling 30-day measurement for internal ops; final credit decisions use UTC calendar month with incident verification
Exclusions: scheduled maintenance windows (see maintenance policy), force majeure, customer-induced network outages, and agreed third-party outages
Scheduled maintenance: quarterly major upgrades + up to 4 hours/month minor maintenance per region; customer requests for blackout windows (trading hours) must be honored where feasible
Emergency maintenance: Redwood to provide 4-hour notice where possible; for P1 security patches could be <4-hour notice but will be communicated to SRE contacts
Support SLAs: Sev1 (platform down or major impact) - initial response <= 60 minutes, mitigation plan within 4 hours; Sev2 - initial response <= 4 hours; Sev3 - next-business-day
Escalation path: AE -> SE -> Escalation Engineer -> Head of Customer Reliability; 24/7 phone for Sev1 included on enterprise tier
Right to audit and telemetry: Auriga requested per-request token-level logs for compliance (redacted PII) and 12-month audit log retention (approved with KMS integration)
Model pinning/rollback: Customer can pin a specific model version per-route; automatic fallback to verified lower-capacity variant allowed only with prior agreement
Capacity reservation: commitment for 8x A100-80GB equivalent GPUs reserved per region (NA/EU) with burst pool of 2 GPUs per region for short-term traffic spikes

Throughput guarantees: baseline concurrency targets provided - 1.2k RPS for embeddings service (batching), 200 concurrent chat sessions with p95 response latency <= 600ms for 64-token responses under normal load
Change control: scheduled major changes require 30-day notice and a coordinated rollback playbook; emergency changes require notification within 2 hours after cutoff
sla_negotiation_notes: Auriga legal pushed back on a flat 99.99% ask — wants granular credits tied to region-specific outages
They insist on explicit measurement methodology (how 'downtime' is computed) — Redwood suggested synthetic probes + customer telemetry reconciliation
Primary concern: maintenance windows overlapping US morning trading hours (13:30-17:30 UTC) — asked for blackout option for critical clusters
Auriga wants credits applied automatically based on telemetry exports (they will not rely only on Redwood tickets) — legal to add API-based evidence submission clause
Discussed carve-outs for planned DR drills; Auriga requested inclusion of DR runbook acceptance criteria before drills count as planned maintenance
Price vs SLA trade-off: Auriga open to a 15% discount in exchange for a 99.9% guaranteed uptime (vs 99.95%) — Redwood pricing team asked for usage history to model economics
Debated support response times: Auriga wants on-site CIRT options for first 90 days of production; Redwood offered dedicated remote warroom with daily syncs
capacity_planning_notes: POC showed p95 token generation at ~420ms for 64-token runs on proposed shard config; further kernel tuning expected to shave ~70-100ms
Recommended reserved config: 2 shards x 4x A100-80GB per shard per region (total 8 GPUs active / region), sync-replicated to meet failover RTO 3 minutes
Burst pool: 2x A100 per region for 30-minute bursts; customer wants pre-warmed instances during major events (quarterly earnings windows)
Network topology: customer requires direct VPC peering to avoid public internet egress during trading hours; egress encryption and dedicated NAT endpoints requested
Batching strategy: embeddings batched to 512 tokens/batch for throughput and cost targets; chat uses smaller adaptive batching to preserve latency SLOs
Capacity runway: initial commit 12 months with quarterly scaling reviews tied to traffic growth and model changes
operational_risks_and_mitigations: Risk: cross-region correlated failure during cloud provider maintenance -> Mitigation: multi-region replication and routing failover policy; runbook tested in POC
Risk: kernel regression after model upgrade -> Mitigation: canary rollout + traffic shadowing and automatic rollback on latency regressions
Risk: network egress and on-prem link flaps -> Mitigation: dual WAN links with BGP failover; heartbeats and automatic draining of in-flight requests
Risk: legal wanting SLA credits as cash refunds -> Mitigation: propose service credits as default; cash refunds only by exec approval
